title: Entice HP+
description:
Entice is CRL's all-glass entrance system, launched in 2015. Customer feedback on the original pointed to air, water and wind-load performance: the center-hung pivot door left a 3/16" gap at the top and bottom of the frame.

Entice HP+ re-engineers the door around a continuous geared hinge and an automatic drop-bottom seal. That closes the gaps, raises structural performance and allows larger doors. I joined the program during development and carried it through launch, the first production order and the post-launch review.

metrics.label: Full-scale structural rating, up from 20 psf

brief.label: Problem
brief.text: The original center-hung Entice door had 3/16" gaps top and bottom, letting air and water through.

brief.label: Solution
brief.text: A continuous geared hinge in place of the pivot, plus an automatic drop-bottom seal. Together they improve sealing and wind-load resistance and allow larger doors.

brief.label: Customers
brief.text: Architects and Division 8 contractors, for commercial offices, government buildings, retail and hospitality.

brief.label: Value
brief.text: For architects: Title 24 viable, high thermal performance, and freedom in scale and aesthetics.

brief.label: Competition
brief.text: U.S. Aluminum Mojave 250T, FHC Aspire, Assa Abloy ThermaGuard.

brief.label: Launch
brief.text: The first order shipped in 27 business days against a 20-day standard. We used it to tighten the production flow for the orders behind it.

challenges.challenge: The first production order shipped in 27 business days against a 20-day standard.
challenges.resolution: We walked the order through the plant with production, documented where it stalled, and tightened the flow so the orders behind it shipped closer to standard.

challenges.challenge: Sales were losing HP+ specifications on projects that needed sidelites and transoms.
challenges.resolution: The Gate 5 review turned that feedback into a funded follow-on program, Entice HP+ Transom and Sidelites.

challenges.challenge: Some HP+ door-rail SKUs were missed during the company's move to SAP, so a few configurations couldn't be ordered.
challenges.resolution: We audited the full configuration list against what existed in SAP and submitted the missing items in one request, rather than discovering them order by order.
